details:
I tried Avatars 3.0 recently, and the interface is really good, but there's one major problem which I think I have a solution for.
The problem is that if you're puppeteering something, like your facial gestures, or a tail or whatever, you can't move with that stick. 
Now, you can of course, walk around the room you're in to move about a bit, but not all of us have a large playspace.
To get to the point, what I propose is to allow the use of the trigger, which is the only button you can really access while also moving the stick, as a momentary button to quickly open the menu, move the stick around, and then release to lock the avatar in whatever facial gesture or pose you selected while in the menu.
I believe as the menu currently operates, it will keep the last menu section you were in active, so this setup would enable you to quickly switch between moving and puppeteering, which I think is an absolute necessity for this method of doing facial gestures to replace the current standard. Otherwise, I feel like avatars will suddenly become a lot less animated in the face, because people will be less inclined to go into the menu often if they have to hold down a button to open it, select the face pose, and then exit it again with another button press. That's simply too much effort compared to a finger point. But pulling the trigger and pushing up at the same time and releasing the trigger again... That's quick and easy to do on the fly.
Of couse this momentary trigger setup may not play nice with the push in a direction then click method of selecting menu items that you made optional, but with the "flick" option, it would work fine.
title: [FEEDBACK] Quick menu access
